name: Screen Time and parental controls
plain: Limits apps and websites and reads usage summaries, with opaque identifiers on iOS.
meaning: Shows app habits; iOS hides which apps behind tokens, Android returns package names.

android.revocation: Settings > Special app access > Usage access
android.store_policy: Play: restricted for parental and wellbeing use
android.note: Android returns package names and times; QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES also restricted

ios.store_policy: Apple approves; apps must follow 5.1.1 kids rules
ios.note: Opaque tokens hide app identity; distribution entitlement needs Apple request

limits.headline: Can limit apps and websites and see usage summaries, once you or a parent allow it
limits.user_action: You approve the Screen Time sheet on iPhone, or turn on Usage access in Settings on Android
can: Set limits on apps and websites
See how long apps were used, by name on Android
Show usage summaries to a parent or to you
cannot: See which apps were used on iPhone; hidden tokens stand in for app names
Ship on iPhone without Apple's family controls entitlement
List every installed app on Android; that permission is restricted
limits.differs: Android returns app names and times; iPhone hides app identity behind tokens.

story.what_it_is: Screen time and parental controls that limit apps and sites and show usage summaries.

marketing.name: Screen Time and parental controls
marketing.pitch: Set limits for apps, websites and communication to help families manage how kids use their devices.

marketing.name: Family Link
marketing.pitch: Set digital ground rules, manage apps and see activity on your child's phone.

story.for_you: You set daily limits and see simple charts of how long each app was used. A child sees a screen asking for more time. Parents can approve in a tap.
story.for_makers: Parental control apps give families a way to manage kids' phones. They need strong access to apps and websites. On iPhone the apps get opaque tokens, not names, so the maker cannot see which apps a child uses.

use_cases.example: A parent limits a child to one hour of games on school nights.
A school sets homework mode that blocks social apps.
A digital wellbeing app shows you how long you used social media today.
A parent sets a bedtime lock on a child's game console style apps.
A teen asks their parent to approve a new chat app.
A parent blocks adult sites for a child.
An adult sets their own limits to reduce doom scrolling.

story.android_note: Android gives parent apps package names and usage times. Access to the full app list is limited by store rules.
story.ios_note: iPhone hides app identity behind opaque tokens. Distributing a parental app needs an Apple request.

technical_bounds: Opaque tokens cannot be mapped to bundle ids
